system.name: EZ-SAVE
system.one_liner: an evaluation of easy-to-deploy source address validation (SAV) policies, including BAR-SAV, against BGP spoofing and false positives

content.subject: how BAR-SAV correctly accepts a Direct-Server-Return response that naive SAV policies would wrongly drop as spoofed

relations.what: AS4 is transit provider for customer AS1
AS4 is transit provider for customer AS2
AS5 is transit provider for customer AS3
AS4 and AS5 are settlement-free peers
AS5 forwards the announcement for 5.6/16 with AS-path 5-3

steps.what: the user (AS1) sends a content request toward the CDN server (AS3)
AS3 tunnels the request onward to the CDN edge server AS2 that will actually serve it
AS2 sends the response data packets (source IP 5.6.7.8, in prefix 5.6/16) toward AS4, which must decide whether to drop them

content.key_idea: Because AS2 holds a ROA for 5.6/16 even without announcing it, BAR-SAV correctly accepts its Direct-Server-Return response that naive SAV policies would wrongly drop as spoofed.
content.reading_order: starts at the policy list top-left, follows Request from AS1 to AS3, the tunneled Request down to AS2, then Legitimate-packets up to AS4's verdict

encoding.color_means: blue = BGP Announcement labels/edges; cyan = the Request/Request(tunneled) flow; orange = the Legitimate-packets response and its source IP; pale blue-lavender = the AS node circles
encoding.line_style_means: solid black lines with a downward arrowhead show provider-customer links, dashed black shows the AS4-AS5 peer link; dashed coloured lines show BGP announcements, solid coloured lines show data/request traffic
encoding.state_means: not applicable (a single scenario, not a before/after or alternatives figure); the accept-vs-drop outcome is instead told apart by a green check next to BAR-SAV versus a red X at AS4 and the red-labelled policy names
encoding.marker_means: a green check mark means BAR-SAV does not drop the packet; a red X at AS4 and the red policy names (FP-uRPF, EFP-A, EFP-B) mean those policies would wrongly drop it
encoding.emphasis: the red X sits exactly where the orange Legitimate-packets arrow reaches AS4, staging the false-positive drop that BAR-SAV alone avoids
reusable_patterns: a small AS-level topology with provider/customer and peer edges plus a distinct arrow colour per traffic type (announcement, request, response), annotated with a pass/fail verdict at the decision point
weaknesses: small (~5pt) prefix/hop-count labels crowd the diagram
reusing similar line styles for both announcement propagation and the physical provider/customer edges can be hard to disentangle at a glance

evidence: BAR-SAV can also avoid false positives when a customer AS uses Direct Server Return (DSR)
Fig. 3 shows an example. AS3 (hosting a CDN server) announces a prefix 5.6/16.
The DSR scenario (see illustration in Fig. 3) includes a CDN server, CDN edge server, and users.

summary: This figure from EZ-SAVE's SAV Policies section walks through a Direct Server Return (DSR) scenario that BAR-SAV must classify as legitimate. A CDN server (AS3, announcing 5.6/16) receives a Request from a user (AS1, 1.2/16) and tunnels it onward to the CDN edge server that will actually respond (AS2, reachable only via 3.4/16). AS2's Legitimate packets (source IP 5.6.7.8) then travel up toward AS4, which must decide whether to drop them. Dashed blue BGP Announcement edges show AS4 only ever learns of prefix 5.6/16 through AS5's path via AS3, never through AS2, so naive filters (FP-uRPF, EFP-A, EFP-B, all in red) would wrongly drop the packet (red X). BAR-SAV instead checks that AS2 holds a ROA authorizing it to originate 5.6/16, even though AS2 never announces it, and correctly accepts the packet (green check).
summary_zh: 该图走读BAR-SAV如何正确处理一次DSR场景：用户请求经AS1到AS3再隧道转发至边缘服务器AS2；AS2发出的合法响应包(源地址5.6.7.8)到达AS4时，朴素SAV策略(FP-uRPF、EFP-A、EFP-B)会将其误丢弃，而BAR-SAV凭借AS2持有的5.6/16号段ROA证明其合法，正确放行(绿色对勾标出)。
notes: content.base and content.groups kept as prior (topology; walkthrough): the arrows are labelled with actions (Request, Request(tunneled), Legitimate packets) rather than drawn circled numbers, matching v3's 'step labels on arrows' walkthrough variant, so layout.step_markers is set to 'labelled-arrows' rather than 'circled-numbers'. style.palette uses exactly the 5 hex values in the index's measured-attributes histogram; a green check mark (BAR-SAV) and a red X / red policy names (FP-uRPF, EFP-A, EFP-B) are clearly visible in the source PNG but fall outside that top-5 list (likely small-area text/icon glyphs below the measurement's area cutoff), so they are described qualitatively in 'encoding' rather than given an asserted exact hex.
